question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations, side pocket (segregated portfolio) treatment is:

answer.text: Mandatory for all Cat I and Cat II AIFs.
Permitted only for Cat III AIFs; NOT typical for Cat I/II.

explanation.text: The Logic: Side pocket / segregated portfolio treatment is the practice of carving out illiquid or distressed holdings into a separate accounting compartment so that valuation and redemption issues do not contaminate the main portfolio. This mechanism is most relevant to open-ended structures that need to allow subscriptions and redemptions at fair NAV. Among the AIF categories, only Category III can be structured open-ended, while Category I and II are close-ended with fixed LP commitments and rely on tenure-based dissolution/in-specie mechanics rather than ongoing redemption — making side pockets typical of Cat III, not Cat I/II. The Trap: "Mandatory for all Cat I/II" overstates the position — side pockets are not a Cat I/II default at all. "Only for Angel Funds" is fabricated. "Automatic for any debt AIF" confuses categories — open-ended Cat III debt structures are the typical home for side-pocket mechanics, not all debt AIFs. Note: The specific rule that side-pocket / segregated-portfolio treatment is permitted only for Category III AIFs and is not typical for Cat I/II is not stated in the cited workbook chapter (24 NISM-Series-XIX-D Category I and II Alternative Investment Fund Managers Certification Examination_January 2026.pdf, pp. 54, 292-295, 333-334), and a text search of that workbook for "side pocket" and "segregated portfolio" did not surface relevant content. The framing above is general industry knowledge of side pockets in open-ended alternative funds.
